 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Chicago Bulls face a brutal test on Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. They arrive with a 1-5 record, while the Philadelphia 76ers sit at 6-1. This gap in the standings tells only half the story. The real issue for Chicago lies in their defense, which allows a league-worst 129.3 points per game, according to Metro Philadelphia. That number is a massive hole that no amount of offense can easily plug.
 Philadelphia boasts the second-best defense in the league, giving up just 104.9 points per contest. The mismatch is stark. The Bulls need a perfect night to stay close, but their current trajectory suggests otherwise. They have lost four straight games, including a 125-111 defeat to the Celtics on Friday night. A team that cannot stop the other side from scoring will struggle against a squad that can.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Shooting Woes Add to the Mess
 Offense is not the savior here either. The Bulls are the league's worst three-point shooting team, hitting only 28.1 percent of their attempts, per Metro Philadelphia. They average 113.5 points per game, which looks fine on paper, but it is not enough against a top-tier defense. Chicago needs their absolute best game of the season just to keep it competitive. They face a 7:30 PM ET tip with little margin for error.
 Their schedule has been unforgiving, featuring losses to the Knicks, Celtics, Raptors, and Wizards. They won just once this season, a 132-125 victory over the Bucks on October 23. That win came against a team with a different defensive profile. The Sixers will not be as forgiving. The Bulls might look at a 1-9 record before they face the Hawks again. The pressure to find an identity is mounting fast.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Embiid Status Looms Large
 The biggest variable for the Sixers is Joel Embiid. He is listed as questionable for Monday due to right foot injury management, per Yahoo Sports . If he sits out, the Bulls have a chance. The 76ers have shown they can win without him, fending off the Hornets 109-104 on Saturday. Tyrese Maxey scored 38 points in that game, proving the team has depth.
 In his career matchups versus Chicago, Embiid has posted averages of 29.3 points and 10.8 rebounds, securing a double-double. He has thrived there in the past. If he plays, the Bulls frontcourt faces a major threat. The Bulls' lone victory came when they could score enough to outpace opponents, but they have not done that recently.
